method: ConvNeXt-Tiny fine-tune (as E6b) + geometric augmentation (h-flip, +-10 deg rotation, 5% shift, 0.9-1.1 scale) + label smoothing 0.1, 15 epochs
explanation: NEGATIVE result: val accuracy 0.944, i.e. -1.5 pts vs E6b (0.959). Augmentation + label smoothing reduced memorisation (train 0.9995, loss plateaus ~0.45 because of smoothing) but hurt generalisation. Errors concentrate on facebook->whatsapp (32 vs fewer in E6b) and mozilla (0.95 -> 0.87). Likely cause: rotation/scale resampling blurs the anti-aliased outlines and gradients that ARE the vendor signature, so the 'invariance' we injected removes discriminative information. Caveat: 3 things changed at once (aug, smoothing, 15 epochs) - effect not attributable to one of them; kept E6b setting (no aug) going forward.
preprocessing: Alpha-composite on white background, then resize to 128 x 128 (bicubic), ImageNet normalisation; train-time random flip/affine (no colour jitter)
preprocessing_why: E6b overfits (train 1.000 vs val 0.959). Geometric augmentation creates plausible variants without touching colour, which is itself a vendor signal; label smoothing discourages over-confident memorisation.
